definitions.explanation: The external appearance or form of something, how it looks on the surface.
The format or layout of a document, book, or other material.
Concern for how one appears to others; maintaining dignity or reputation in social situations.

examples.japanese: {体裁|ていさい}を{整|ととの}える
とりあえず{体裁|ていさい}だけは{整|ととの}えた。
examples.english: For now, I at least got it into proper form.

examples.japanese: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}の{体裁|ていさい}
{この|この}{体裁|ていさい}で{提出|ていしゅつ}してください。
examples.english: Please submit it in this format.

examples.japanese: {書式|しょしき}の{体裁|ていさい}を{統一|とういつ}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to standardize the document format.

examples.japanese: {体裁|ていさい}を{気|き}にする
{体裁|ていさい}ばかり{気|き}にしていると、{本質|ほんしつ}を{見失|みうしな}う。
examples.english: If you only care about appearances, you'll lose sight of what really matters.

notes:
USAGE: The meaning depends on context. In formal or business settings, often refers to format (sense 2). In social contexts, often relates to keeping up appearances (sense 3).

NUANCE: When used about social situations (sense 3), {体裁|ていさい} can have negative connotations of being overly concerned with superficial appearances rather than substance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体裁|ていさい}を{整|ととの}える (to put in proper form)
- {体裁|ていさい}が{良|よ}い/{悪|わる}い (looks good/bad)
- {体裁|ていさい}を{気|き}にする (to care about appearances)
- ～の{体裁|ていさい} (the format of ~)

RELATED WORDS:
- {世間体|せけんてい} (reputation, appearances to others)
- {面目|めんぼく} (face, honor)
- {書式|しょしき} (format - documents only)
